utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Before the witness is brought in, I should like to ask you to allow our Defence team member, Jonathan Flynn to attend the hearing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We certainly would allow that, and welcome. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would remind you of the affirmation you made to tell the truth which still applies, and we continue now your evidence and invite Mr. Stamp to ask any questions he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milasinovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was looking at your curriculum vitae, and I see it says in your career resume that in 1972 you were employed at the Ministry of Interior Affairs for the socialist Republic of Serbia, and then in 1973 to 1988 you were employed in the federal Ministry of Interior. You worked for a year in 1972 at the Ministry of Interior for Serbia, Republic of Serbia; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, I also worked for the republican Ministry of the Interior in Croatia for three years, so that I spent the total of five years as a staff member of a republican ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Because the transcripts seem to reflect that you were saying that you worked three years in the MUP Republic of Serbia, so that is not correct. You worked one year in the MUP Republic of Serbia and three years in the MUP Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked for two and a half years for the republican MUP of Serbia and three and a half years for the republican MUP of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. When did you work for the republican MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked for the Croatian MUP from the 1st or the 15th of January, 1988 up until November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When did you work for the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 10th of January, 1992, up until the 15th of May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you open your curriculum vitae. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Can you have a look at your curriculum vitae, please. I think in line 20 -- oh, let me just ask the witness. You started working in the MUP Republic of Serbia in 1972; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 10th of January, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, I should not be interfering at this point, but can you repeat the question because apparently there's been a mistake as far as the years are concerned, and we are wasting time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, there certainly seems to be some difference between the printed document and the spoken evidence of the witness. If you think it's important, you better clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your curriculum vitae indicates that you worked for the Ministry of Interior or interior affairs socialist Republic of Serbia 1972, and not from January 1972 to May 1994, as you now claim. Which is correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I worked from the 10th of January, 19 -- 1972 up until the 15th of May, 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So what is printed there in your curriculum vitae is not correct, or at least incomplete?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be incomplete, and it is possible that there may be a mistake, but what I'm saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: All right. If I tell you that your curriculum vitae published on the website for the university of Belgrade also indicates that you worked in the MUP Serbia only during the year of 1972, would that refresh your memory as to when you worked in the MUP for Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That curriculum vitae was drafted by a staff member who did not consult me directly but drew upon incomplete information contained in various documents. You see, some of my documents were left behind in Ljubljana and Zagreb, and it is possible that he may have made some mistakes in drafting my CV.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. But at least with the CV that we have here, I saw yesterday, and I feel very certain that counsel for Mr. Djordjevic did give you an opportunity to correct your CV, but you didn't make use of the opportunity. Is there any reason why?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use the opportunity simply because I was giving an overview of all the posts I held in both the republican MUP of Serbia and the federal MUP, so I didn't think that the various dates of -- in terms of office were important. But you can see that I spent the total of five years, at least five years working for the republican ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you are telling us now that you also worked for the republican Ministry of the Interior in Croatia. Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the whole of 1999, 1990 and 1991 up until November -- or rather, from 1998 when I was employed there, that was when I started working for the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I see here it says from 1998 when I was employed there. Can you say again --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1998, yes. From the end of 1998 and the start of 1999 up until November 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it perhaps 1989 rather than 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1989, apologies. 1989 and 1990 and 1991 through to almost the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What position did you hold in the MUP Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a lecturer on the subject of security and international relations at the faculty of criminal sciences which was initially part of the republican Ministry of the Interior and eventually it became part of the Zagreb university.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. What position did you hold in the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, I performed tasks of operative nature aimed at uncovering and suppressing individuals engaged in anti-constitutional activities, or activities against the constitutional order of the Republic of Serbia. So they were of an operative nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: By operative nature, you mean that you were involved in gathering information from persons in the field?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What do you mean by operative nature?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant to say that I first underwent a specialised training and took a number of exams which had to do with the workings of the internal agencies of the Republic of Serbia. Thereupon I was assigned to deal with the suppression of activities aimed at overthrowing the constitutional order or disrupting the constitutional order. These were tasks that had to do both with state security and public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you employed in state security or in public security or in both?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an employee of the state security of the republican ministry. Now, in the federal ministry I was head of the information and analysis department which post I held from 1994 to 1998, and there I had tasks pertaining to both public and state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You have to try to slow down when you speak of dates, Mr. Milasinovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, I give you the dates as far as I can remember them. It is difficult to recall each and every date of the activities I performed in the 40 years of my career. I've given you roughly the extent of the posts I held and the time periods concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, but it says here that you claim that you were in the federal ministry from 1994 to 1998. Are you actually saying that you were there from 1974 until 1988?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I said that I was head of the department for research, analysis, and information from 1984, and previously I was charged with performing other sort of duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, line 6, but I can't tell which page it was, the witness said from 1984 to 1988 and what we have in the transcript is 1994 and 1998, so we have confusion again. That's page 6, line 1. He said from 1984 to 1988 and not from 1994 to 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, in any case, I think I clarified that because later on he said 1974 to 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Milasinovic, let's just cut this down. Have you ever been employed in the public service department of the Ministry of the Interior for the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia comprised both the public security and state security departments, their competences overlapped. Therefore, their activities overlapped insofar as when I was working for the state security, I also did some tasks that came under the competence of public security. However, when I said that I was working for the republican ministry, I said that I was discharging duties falling under state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let me be clear about this. Did you ever have the employment status of being a member of the public security for the Republic of Serbia? Were you employed within the Republic of Serbia MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for that department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 3 of your curriculum vitae in English under your most important papers, and this is going to your academic career and some of your published books, these are quite impressive list of publications involving intelligence services and the activities of these intelligence services international affairs, especially aimed against the FRY. I probably missed any that dealt specifically with the organisation of the MUP for the Republic of Serbia. Among your most important papers, have you published any work in any serious journal on the organisation of the MUP for the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but let me correct you first in one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, corrections can come later. Questions can be asked from different parties. I have limited time. Where on your curriculum vitae, you have it in front of you, is that important work on the publication on the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia? Look at your curriculum vitae, please, that's what I'm asking you, and find it, and tell us where it is, if it is here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sources and Forms of Threatening the Security of SFRY." That was one paper that was published. I don't know if it's included here. I've already told you who it was who drafted this. Secondly, the role -- "The Place and Role of State Security Organs in Suppressing Crime in the Republic of Serbia." Another thing that is not mentioned here is that I was project manager on the subject of the role of the organs of Internal Affairs in the Republic of Serbia in the activities against threats to the security of the Republic of Croatia -- of Serbia. What is also not included is that I had a consultative role that I played on several occasions on some of these subjects, so what is stated here is most of the work I've done, but there were also projects of an internal character that were used by organisational units of all the republics and provinces which explained the organisation and workings of the organs of Internal Affairs. They were also used by some educational institutions --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, time is limited. Do not waste time and do not evade the questions. Please look at your CV and point to us, if you can, at any publication by you relating to the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a collection of papers for criminological and sociological research.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, look at your CV --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm doing. And item -- collection of papers. It's under 12, collection of papers for criminological and sociological research, and the paper was "Role of the Organs of Interior Internal Affairs in Crime Prevention."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about crime prevention or criminology or anything like that. I'm asking you about the organisation of the MUP of Serbia. Have you published anything relating to the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that particular work, that's what -- that's the one that deals with the organisation of the MUP of Serbia precisely. And apart from that, I lectured on subjects related to security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not asking about security. I'm asking you now about your curriculum vitae. Is there anything else on your curriculum vitae in terms of your publications that you say relates to the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just part of the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I take it then --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of my work put on that list. It's not here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So apart from this work on crime prevention, there's nothing here relating to the organisation of the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this list, no, but I did have such papers --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is there anything -- why, Mr. Milasinovic, you are here presenting this document relating to the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia and in your CV listing your publications you do not include your publications on the management or the organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that wasn't what I was asked to do. And I explained what I did yesterday, and apart from that, the works published here and listed here is not part of the work of the intelligence services aimed against Yugoslavia but about the work of the intelligence services in general in the world, and you can see that from the title, from the title of those various papers and work, and none of them relate to intelligence work against Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Specifically the title of this document that you have presented to the court, "The Position and Role of the Chief of the Public Security Department in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in the Anti-terrorist Activities in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999." That's specifically what you title it. And I take it that you would agree with me that you have never published anything in the past on the management, organisation of the MUP Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not publish them in scientific and scholarly journals, but I did work on the projects that were used in the organs of the interior and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did you publish them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was published -- well, they were internal studies to do with internal projects used -- well, in all the republics and provinces. They were published for the internal requirements, for instance, in the security institute, they were printed in Zagreb, in Belgrade, Ljubljana, Skopje, all over. They were printed and published for the purposes of the Internal Affairs organs and for training and educational purposes in the organs and institutions of the Internal Affairs organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again, I was asking you about publications in scholarly publications, but you are telling us now that they are internal documents. This is not disclosed in your curriculum vitae. You are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am conscious of the fact that not all of the papers that were published are listed here, but you can check that out. You can verify the fact that I did have work published in the various collections of works, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It should be reflected in your CV, Mr. Milasinovic, and I represent to you that you have never published any work in any scholarly publication in respect to the management, organisation of the MUP Serbia before this document that you bring before this court, never.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994 I did publish a paper of that kind, and you can check that out. You'll find it in the collection of crime and sociological institutions for the institute for sociological research, and the contents of that paper of mine can be found in that collection of crime-related papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Milasinovic, that the Prosecution had filed a motion claiming that you were not an expert in the field of the leadership responsibilities in the MUP Serbia? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that was, you know, months ago. Having been aware of that, Mr. Milasinovic, did you not think it was important to indicate on your CV that you had done or prepared some of these unpublished works on the leadership and management responsibilities of the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did state that I attended a specialist course dealing with the organisation of --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Don't evade the question.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as far as scholarly and scientific papers are concerned, I did not list that for the simple reason that, as far as these requirements go and what was needed here, only the data that was taken off the internet site from the faculty of security were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's move on. Did you write this report with any assistance, or did you receive assistance in writing it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- well, the final version, yes, but in the initial work I engaged over 50 people who assisted me in compiling this, in compiling this expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were any of those 50 people employed to the BIA in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all worked in the military security organs in the public security sector and the state security sector, and some of them were in special units whereas there were also people from scientific institutions and from the university as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we look at one or two aspects of your report because it seems that you've made quite a few statements in the report which don't seem to be supported. If we look at page 10 in the English version of your report.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you are referring to what? The special-purpose units?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does that refer to the special units and groups, the SAJ and the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me find --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please. It's in -- yes, it's at page 12 in English, I'm sorry, and it's under the paragraph that is numbered 2.2.3, and it is the third to last paragraph in that section, the third to last paragraph before section 2.3.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Third to last paragraph before paragraph 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that's being located, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can't be giving references in English. Mr. Stamp must give us the reference in the Serbian version because the pages are different in Serbian, the number of pages are different in Serbian than English. So we are not able to pin-point the reference. What does he mean, paragraph 2.3 of what? Could he give us the Serbian reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are not the paragraph numbers the same? Not the page numbers, but the paragraph numbers? He was giving paragraph numbers, so that ought to be -- but, thank you, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I'm told it's page 12 in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But, I think, Mr. Milasinovic, it would be easier to find if you use your own numbering system. You have a section that is 2.3. If you look three paragraphs before that, you see a paragraph which reads: "The SAJ belonged to the category of special purpose police units, smaller in strength, up to 200 members but highly homogenised and permanently mobile. The personnel consisting of highly professional, highly organised, specialised and well-equipped police officers.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stamp not read so fast please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Had undergone a strict selection process.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last section reads: "Their engagement in the performance of special purpose tasks could be ordered only by the minister or by a chief authorised by the minister." You make that statement and there is no support for that statement in your report. What was the source or on what material did you base this statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based it on the decision on establishing the SAJ in 1996 from the 5th of April, dated the 5th of April, which refers to the SAJ and the characteristics and nature of those special anti-terrorist units, the SAJ which existed in the previous period as well in 199 -- well, before 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So are you saying that the document forming the SAJ stated that only the minister or the chief authorising the minister could engage the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only the minister that can issue orders of that nature. And pursuant to an order from the minister or permission from the minister, somebody else could take it up down the chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's what you said. Listen to the question I'm asking you about the basis for saying that. Are you saying that you made this statement because that is what the document on the formation of the SAJ stated?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document and decision on the establishment of the SAJ, but it also refers to the rights and duties of the minister as the sole elected individual by the National Assembly into the Ministry of the Interior, also refers to those documents. And he was the sole person who had the authority to organise the special units, the SAJs and PJPs within the organs of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you did not cite that document when you made that statement, why you did not give us a footnote indicating that that was the reference and that was the basis on which you made that statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is stipulated in the earlier observation, so I didn't think I needed to repeat it again to repeat the same sources again, because if you read the document carefully, you would be able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Where in the earlier observations did you make that statement and provide a reference?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Article 7 of the Law on Internal Affairs which is mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, we can't be going all over the place --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I read to you a sentence and I asked you what was the source. You said the source was a document on the formation of the SAJ. I want you to show us where it is that you made that statement in the report and cited that source document on the formation of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the decision by the minister on the establishment of the SAJ. Let me just take a moment to locate that passage. The number is 1693/96, the 5th of April, 1996. That's the date of it. That's the date of that decision. It's on page 12, the decision on the establishment of the SAJ. The decision on the establishment of the SAJ, number 1693/96 of the 5th of April, 1996. Article 6, para 2, the Law on Internal Affairs, you'll find it there too. Formed by the minister, by decision, that is to say the minister of the interior, on the basis of the laws that were valid at the time governing the Ministry of the Interior and the rules on internal MUP organisation, and then a decision on the establishment of the SAJ 1693/96 of the 5th of April, 1996. Decision on the establishment of the SAJ. So there you have four sources, all of these relate to this observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you are telling us it's a decision on the formation of the SAJ. Let's look at that one, that's D401. Could we look at it quickly. D401 is a decision on the establishment of the SAJ. I'm going to represent to you that it does not say what you stated before the court that it says. If you can find where it says that only the minister or the chief of public security authorised by the minister could engage the SAJ, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this decision, the special SAJ unit is established as a separate unit so that all the tasks can reflect the requirements of everyone on the basis of Article 6, para 2 of the "Official Gazette" of Serbia, 1991. Article 6, para 1 of the Laws on the Internal Organisation of the Ministry of the Interior, and may we turn the page, please. Next page, please, if possible. Signed by minister Sokolovic. So everything that I have just talked about is set out there, and it refers to the nature of the SAJs themselves and their characteristic features. So this observation --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe there was a misunderstanding. Let's do it again. You make the statement that engagement of the SAJ in the performance of special purpose tasks could be ordered only by the minister or by the chief authorised by the minister. And when I asked you on what basis you made that, you said on the basis of this decision. I'm asking you where it is in this decision, what is it about this decision? Point to us what it is about this decision that caused you or that supports that statement. It's a short decision, tell us which statement or which paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was supported by Article 7 of the Law on the Interior and Article 6 as well of the rules, and it refers to the decision made by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Excuse me. You will now agree with me, Mr. Milasinovic, that this statement here which is not supported in your report, is certainly not supported by this order or this decision of the minister?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the decision emanates from the authority of the minister and the authority of the minister is vested in the law governing ministries as an organ of statement administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you are now saying --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's a broader base, but I'm talking about the decision which is based on the authority given the minister by the laws of the country and passed by the National Assembly as the source authority based on the law governing Internal Affairs and authority stemming from the rules on organisation for the organs of the interior, and the possibility of forming and establishing the SAJs and PJPs in the Ministry of the Interior in addition to the regular units and organisational forms within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm being very precise.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So they are based on the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sir, I'm being very precise. You are saying that the rules of internal organisation of the MUP, Article 7, and the law of Internal Affairs, Article 6, also support that statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 6, para 1 of the Rules on Internal Organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We'll get back to that. Let's have a look at page 13 on the section 2.4 reserve police squads and local security. And let's look at the third paragraph in that section. Last two sentences.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... were not permanently assigned to them, they were ad hoc units. Once the general mobilisation was declared, their members were signed to appropriate military and police units in accordance with their war time assignments. Again that's a statement for which you have provided no support. What is the basis for that statement? I'm just speaking about the members were assigned to appropriate military police units in accordance with their war time assignments?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I came on the basis of regular procedure during conflicts or imminent danger of war, when it was customary for the reserve police departments and squads to be made up by the reserve force of the military territorial organs and armed as well. And it used to be a social self-protection, a total social self-protection in Yugoslavia before. Here we see it's a question of military and territorial departments and the reserve police force, and this is determined according to their place of residence, and that was the reason for these reserve police departments to be formed to act as a defensive in the various localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So, I take it that your answer, if you are going to answer me precisely and directly as to the basis of the statement, is regular procedure during conflict, that is what your source for making the statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On what basis was that statement made?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a recitive [as interpreted] only, something that remained of the earlier practice applied in all the crisis situations from an era that I experienced and remember. It was stated on the basis of something that used to be a practice, and a direct basis can be found in the rules governing the internal organisation of the MUP, although these are reserve squads which until such point as they are engaged and activated, are not part of the organs of internal affairs. In other words, they are not a component part of them until such time as they are deployed and engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry to have to keep interrupting you, Mr. Milasinovic, but you are an expert supposedly. You can just answer questions. I'm just ask you about the source of the information or the information on which you base the statement. Can I ask you this: When you say that they on general mobilisation the members of the RPOs were assigned to appropriate military and police units, are you saying that the RPOs were disbanded on mobilisation? Or what became of the RPOs, according to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I proceeded from the factual situation. Secondly, as soon as they are mobilised, they are part of the regular police force. In this particular instance, they are not a component part of the MUP. They are merely a defensive force out in the field. There are active policemen appointed to be in command of them because this was dictated by the situation since these operational pursuit groups, they don't have adequate communication systems, so they needed to be supported by the active police force. They lacked proper communication system between various localities. You will know that in Kosovo Metohija, the atmosphere that prevailed is one that you are well informed of according to security assessments. It was necessary under the circumstances to mount a defensive resistance to the attacks by terrorists and other subversive elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In other words, it was a defensive protection accorded to the non-Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You say that these operational groups did not have adequate communication systems, that was a part of your answer. Were these RPOs operational groups? It's at line 20 -- at page 20, line 8, you said: "There are active policemen appointed to be in command of them because this was dictated by the situation since these operational groups, they don't have adequate communication systems." Were these RPOs operational groups?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to -- no, they were not operational groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were PJPs, Posebne special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The RPOs were PJPs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RPOs were part of PJPs, however, the RPO was not a part of operational pursuit groups. If you are referring to operational pursuit groups, then they were part of Special Police Units. In other words, PJPs; whereas, the RPOs did not hold the status of members of the MUP up until the point of their deployment, engagement, or mobilisation into the regular police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. So you are saying -- I'm reading now what you just said. They were part of the PJPs, however, they were not part of the operational pursuit groups. Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RPOs were not a part of the regular police units. That's a mistake. I may have misspoken. If I said that, it was a mistake on my part. The reserve police squads are not part of the regular police force. What I thought you were asking me about were operational pursuit groups, operational pursuit squads. I thought you were asking me about the squads of pursuit groups. They were part of the police force, but not the RPOs, the reserve police squads. They had nothing to do with the regular or Special Police unions, and can you please have that corrected because I either misunderstood or misspoke or it was not recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's get back to the statement in your report that the members were assigned to appropriate military police units in accordance with war time assignments on general mobilisation. And the question is this: On general mobilisation, were the RPOs disbanded, or did they remain in existence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the military conscripts would, based on their war time assignments, report either to reserve police units or military police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay, simple question --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as to whether they would be disbanded or not, this is a different issue which would depend most probably on the security assessment. The RPOs were comprised armed members of the reserve forces of the military territorial organs and the reserve police force. In the event of mobilisation, they would be deployed to the localities as defined in their war time assignments. And they could simply not, in this sense, be able to operate as reserve police squads in different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I'm asking a question again for the third time. Having regard to what you said here, is it that on general mobilisation, the RPOs were disbanded because their members were assigned to the appropriate military or police units, or did the RPOs remain in existence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it was precisely the individuals who had war time assignments would join -- would be members of the reserve police squad, for this very reason, the RPOs could not remain in existence for the purposes for which they were initially put together. They could not remain in existence because they were composed of military territorial, or rather, the reserve force of the military territorial organs and the reserve police force according to their place of residence. In other words, these were not individuals who arrived from elsewhere. They were locals who were given the possibility of self-defence in the event of an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you just stick to my questions. This statement that you made in your report, which you said is based on your practical experience, and the statement that you make now, which you say could not remain in existence, I am going to ask what's the basis, on what information do you say that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the practice and everything that took place in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who informed you of the practice that took place?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I tasked 50 individuals to research this, and they were supervised by their mentor and the president of the commission. They were the ones researching the subject, and these were researchers, scholars who were tasked with providing me with a detailed explanation of the workings of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You know, it's no where in your report do you tell us that you had these 50 people from state security and military security helping you with your research. You should have told us about this, I put it to you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from state security, but from the public security department. Most of them came from the public security department, and some of them came from the military and state security department. However, 90 per cent of these individuals were from public security departments at all levels post-graduate, graduate, masters, and doctoral research.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's not the point, Mr. Milasinovic. Don't you think that somewhere in your report you should have informed us that many of these statements, and I represent to you that this report is replete with unsupported statements, don't you think you should have told us that you were receiving information from these sources?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have cited that, but I did not necessarily have to cite everything, all the sources of my knowledge. I also toured there -- the various areas of Kosovo and Metohija, interviewed people, and the interviewees were Albanians, Serbs, and non-Albanians. So I was very familiar with these subjects, and not everything I stated in the report needed to have a footnote.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, you did not tell us also that you toured Kosovo and received information that you put in your report. But when did you tour Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I toured it in January of 2006 and in 2007. In other words, a year and a half ago. 1998. And so it was in 2008, I'm sorry. And I was in Kosovo in the earlier years as well. In 1992 I was elected a professor at the Kosovo university, so I had dealings there between 1981 and 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm talking about information that you said you put in this report which is unsourced. When did you tour Kosovo? You said you toured Kosovo and interviewed these people in 2006, 2007, 2008. For what purpose? What assignment were you undertaking when you toured Kosovo in 2006, 2007, 2008 to interview people?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a questionnaire that I had or a poll. It was more of a conversation, an interview I held with people about the events in Kosovo during those war time years. It wasn't a real survey. It was merely for me to gain insight into some of these issues that existed out in the field, that existed in reality rather than drawing upon sources which did not fully reflect the events. I'm not saying that either side is right --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal principles, all the principles of work ethics would not allow me to take sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Try to keep your answers short and direct. These tours of Kosovo when you interviewed people, were they for just out of your personal interest as seems to be indicated by your last answer, or were you undertaking an assignment as an employee or representative of anyone?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't anyone's representative. It was my personal interest in that, and the purpose was to produce a more adequate analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When were you engaged to do this analysis, this one that you have brought before the Court?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was engaged roughly 18 months ago. I'm not sure of the exact time. Perhaps 14, 15 months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 2009 or 2008. I don't remember exactly, and please don't pin me down on any dates because I'm not good on dates. So it was a year and a half ago, roughly. At any rate, before my departure to Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you were engaged to create this report, had this trial started?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trial had already started. I don't know when exactly I was engaged, but I've been working on the analysis for at least a year. So I had been working for a year roughly, and I must have been engaged earlier on. June of 1999. I went to Kosovo on several occasions, and I know that I went there once I was -- I took up this assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So 13 or 14 months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This trial started last year, 2009, you know. So you are telling us --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2009. Which month?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't recall. But you were telling us that you were going to Kosovo in 2006, 2007, 2008 to interview people for this report.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was when I went to Kosovo, but it was only after I took over this assignment of producing the analysis, and that was in January 2009, yes, right. It was the last time I visited Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look quickly at P771.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While it comes up -- while the document comes up I just submit to you -- or not submit, I put to you that you are not correct when you say that these RPOs went out of existence because their members were assigned to the military or police units. This is the minutes of a MUP staff meeting of the 7th of May, 1999 after the general mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The second to last bullet point, and I think you can see from your copy in Serbian that this is General Lukic speaking. He says: "Members of the RPOs must not wear police uniforms, and this must be prohibited immediately except when they have been engaged according to the plan in the reserve police. This must also be applied to military uniforms and ensure that RPO members wear military uniforms only when they are engaged as part of the VJ reserve complement."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could look at another document. P764.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. As soon as general mobilisation was called, their members were assigned to appropriate military or police units based on their war time assignment. We need to bear this in mind as it is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this is -- these are the minutes of the MUP staff meeting of the 4th of April, 1999. And if we go to page 3 in both English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Under item 2, fifth bullet point, Sreten Lukic instructs: "Use ammunition and mines and explosives very rationally and especially draw attention of RPO commanders." Now, having seen those two documents, and let me refer you again to what you said based on your report, this is at page 23, line 5. You said, the RPOs could not -- sorry. Page 22, lines 19 to 21 you said, the RPOs could not remain in existence. That is your evidence here and that is based on this report that is unsourced. Can I ask you, if, according to you the RPOs could not remain in existence after mobilisation, what is General Lukic referring to at these two MUP staff meetings when he speaks about the RPOs and their commanders?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the laws of physics one cannot be in two places at the same time. Those who were mobilised could no longer be members of the RPOs in the place where they were deployed. They were mobilised and therefore had to report to the point of assembly based on their war time assignment, so this would be contrary to the logic and laws of physics. What General Lukic meant when he said this is something that he should be asked about. But it's simply, if someone is mobilised and assigned accordingly, he can only be in that particular location to which he was deployed pursuant to his assignment. There could be armed people left behind who didn't have war time assignments, however, what we see here are individuals who were military conscripts whilst members of the RPOs, but they were at the same time reservists of either the police or the army. You simply can't have one individual in two places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, that's a conclusion you draw, as you say, on the laws of physics. But you have no explanation as to why after general mobilisation General Lukic, the chief of the staff, would be referring to the RPOs and their commanders and giving instructions with respect to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was probably referring to some individuals who stayed behind. I don't know. But it definitely did not refer to what I was talking about, i.e., the RPOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on quickly to page 16 of your report. This is another statement that I will represent to you you have not supported, just an unfounded, unsupported statement that you made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Page 16 in English and it's -- in B/C/S it's three paragraphs before your section 3.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Paragraph entitled "Response to Terrorist Acts."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a short paragraph so I'll just read it in full. Or I'll just start with the second sentence of that paragraph. "In the period starting with the arrival of the Verification Mission and ending with the war, in full compliance with the agreement, the police refrained from anti-terrorist actions and in most cases merely responded to terrorist attacks." This is another, in the context of this case, relatively important statement. On what basis, what was the source of your information to make the statement A, that they were in full compliance with the agreement in respect to the Verification Missions and two, they refrained from anti-terrorist actions and merely responded to terrorist attacks? You have given no citation, you have not told us where you got that information from.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an agreement reached with --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, just a minute --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- one side, that is to say the Serb side --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't want you to tell us about verification agreements, that's not what I'm asking you. I just read to you the statement you made and I'm asking you simply, what was the source of the information that you base this statement on?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source of information was the knowledge that this was not applied. Through interviews we learned this and general knowledge, that the number of units was reduced and that it was only when there was a specific terrorist attack underway that they responded to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Stop there. Please don't repeat what you say. The question is source. I take it your source is interviews?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who did you interview? Start with the interviews. Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direct participants told me. They told me that they did not launch anti-terrorist actions after an agreement was reached between the parties and that they withdrew the heavy weapons, reduced the number of units --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, therefore, did not want to provoke any further incidents in Kosovo, so it stems from the agreement that was respected on all counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question again, I remind you I'm asking you about the source of your information. So you say you interviewed the participants, and they told you they were respecting the agreement. Which participants did you interview in order to make this statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first of all read the agreement and then I went ahead and interviewed quite a number of people. I really can't give you the names now. They were some of my students that were doing specialist training for their MAs, PhDs, and so on that were well versed in those affairs. So there were written documents. I became acquainted with the agreement, and of course then there was practice as well, standard practice and what was done and that testifies to the truth and correctness of this assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you can't help us with the names?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's based on my personal knowledge, what I personally wrote. Well, I can help you out, but I can't tell you their names, and their papers are found in the faculty for security, and they used customary methodology to establish facts for the commission when defending their MA thesis or PhD thesis, and it was papers written for that period, and this gave me a general insight into the situation in Kosovo and Metohija as well as the interviews I had with people, the people I talked to there concerned in these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the next question is going to be, which commission are you speaking of, but I see, Your Honours, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ask that question because if you don't, I was about to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But will we take the break or will we proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ask what the commission is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, which commission, for the second or third time you keep referring to, that assisted you in establishing these facts?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were scientific and tuitional commissions, teaching commissions assessing the exactness and truthfulness of the facts presented in the MA thesis of the various people and their PhD thesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I wonder if we could take the break, and I could consider whether I should follow it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And there was a reference earlier to the president of the commission, which I think needs to be identified as well. But we will have our first break now and resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, very quickly if we can, you said you had -- there were some persons, possibly 50 engaged in research assisting you in setting the facts, and they were in a commission. Who was the president of this commission?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases I was the president of the commission, a member of the commission, or one of the mentors. It was the political science faculty, the police academy, and crime institute and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So there was a commission set up that was staffed or that included members from those three bodies that you have mentioned. When was this commission set up?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission was -- well, actually, it was an ad hoc commission, and commissions linked to a special problem. They were scientific commissions, the faculties proposed commissions, and a council of experts of the university in Belgrade finally elects them. Scientific professional council in Belgrade co-ordinating the work of all the faculties of the Belgrade university.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the commissions that were set up in respect to your evidence. You said that you had information that you received from 50 persons that you tasked who were members of these commissions. When was the commission in respect to your evidence first set up?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were different commissions made up of the best people in the field of terrorism and anti-terrorism in the country. They were ad hoc commissions. It wasn't just one commission. They were ad hoc commissions set up, and for every candidate that was a separate commission, but I am just referring to the commissions in which I was at one time the president, a member, or a mentor of the commission. And they are different degrees of education. MA studies, PhD studies and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Let's turn to your report where we last left off. We were at page 16 where you said the police refrain from anti-terrorist actions in full compliance with the agreement and in most cases may have responded to terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we have a look at P689.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the reference for my version is where?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This was the last part of your report that we were discussing. This is the third to last paragraph before your section 3.2 where you said: "In the period starting with the arrival of the Verification Mission and ending with the war, in full compliance with the agreement, the police refrain from anti-terrorist actions." It's on page 16 in the English version. I want to show you, Mr. Milasinovic, a document which reflects or in which a record was taken of a MUP staff meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to the next page, please. MUP staff meeting on the 2nd of December in Pristina. I think we should move to the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You can see here it's dated the 2nd of December.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's the minutes from the staff meeting, staff members meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the paragraph -- the first paragraph after it says, "the meeting commenced at 1100 hours." In it Major General Lukic briefed the participants on a meeting held in Belgrade by the minister of interior attended by the minister, the chiefs of the departments in which the current security situation in Kosovo was examined and which the duties and further engagement of members of the police of Kosovo were defined. The essence of the meeting was a continued execution of anti-terrorist actions aimed at suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and that in this regard, the police will be more offensive in taking measures in the newly arisen situation. Having regard to the contemporary record of what the head of the MUP staff was saying at that time, would you now agree with me that your statement in your report based on this information you gathered from your researchers that the police refrained from anti-terrorist actions in that period is not correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is -- well, what I said is correct for the simple reason that concrete terrorist activities were reacted to so it was linked, any action was linked to concrete terrorist action, reaction to specific anti-terrorist actions, not broader operations on general anti-terrorist activities. And this, probably although I can't comment the statement made by the general, by General Sreten Lukic, but anyway, I can't say what he was specifically referring to, but certainly you cannot draw the conclusion that after the agreement actions could be intensified, so that's not true, they weren't intensified.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you are saying the police refrained from anti-terrorist actions. That doesn't square up with the contemporary record.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they refrained from carrying out planned actions undertaking the kind of actions that they had undertaken previously. But they reacted to concrete terrorist actions, so there wasn't any planning. It wasn't a planned anti-terrorist action. It was -- it just stated that they needed to intensify standing up and reacting to concrete specific terrorist acts, that's my understanding of this. And to be quite frank, perhaps General Lukic had something else in mind as well when he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The thing is, Mr. Milasinovic, is that you weren't there at the time and you make these sweeping statements without giving us a source of this information except that it is composed of research personnel. Did you see this document before? Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen all the documents before, and I interpret them in a way that corresponds to the actual facts, and the facts are that there was no planning of anti-terrorist activities because a war conflict was expected, or rather, an aggression. So nobody in their right mind would have been able to undertake any widespread activities across the board in quantitative terms because certain forces were withdrawn as were weapons and everything else that was linked to broad anti-terrorist operations. I know that for a fact, and I became aware of it based on many documents speaking to the issue, and also what was done on the ground with the forces, police forces, the police forces of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You must have heard of the Racak anti-terrorist action. Was that one planned, or was it not planned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was planned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terrorist activities on the part of the terrorist organisations and groups and individuals in Kosovo and Metohija were intensified precisely after the arrival of the Verification Commission in October. So as to Racak, yes, I didn't deal with Racak separately in my analysis, and that can be seen from the analysis itself. So that I can't talk about Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also say at page 32 of your report that the MUP staff did not inform the headquarters about anti-terrorist actions. We could keep the document here, but if you could look at page 32 of the report, if you could look at the last paragraph of part 2 of your report.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 32, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, that's the page in English. I'm telling you in Serbian it's the last paragraph of part 2, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The paragraph immediately before part 3 begins.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But what page is it in Serbian, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't assist you. I was using your numbering system, your system of marking it. Mr. Milasinovic, you have part 3 in your report, can't you find that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, part 3. Status, rights, and responsibilities of MUP personnel. Are you referring to part 3, page 32, the status, rights, and responsibilities of MUP personnel; is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to the paragraph immediately before that begins. The last paragraph in part 2. And it's page 31 in Serbian. You say here the secretariats of Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You say here that the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija and the MUP staff did not inform the MUP on a daily basis about these events, and the events we are talking about is anti-terrorist actions. This statement you made that the MUP headquarters was not informed, again, can I take it that you received this information from the research of this commission, because I don't see the basis on which you make this statement cited here? The question is, what was the source of this statement that the MUP staff headquarters were not informed of the anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretariat of the interior on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and the centres of the public security sectors, the staff which was established by the minister was informed about the issues set out here, but it was not -- but the Ministry of the Interior was not informed. So only the minister of the interior could have been informed by the Chief of Staff for anti-terrorist action in Kosovo and Metohija. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are repeating, Mr. Milasinovic. I have to stop you. You are repeating what you said in evidence before and what you have said in the report. I'm pointing you now to this specific part of the report and asking you, what is the source or the basis for making this statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source is to be found in the documents. Whether staff makes it incumbent upon the secretariats and centres to supply them alone with reports on terrorist activities that were planned and carried out and the planned and carried out anti-terrorist actions their results and consequences and the movements of police units in Kosovo and Metohija as well as the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija and the MUP staff, they were -- they did not send daily reports to the MUP. So it's based on the document which the staff forwarded to the secretariats of the Internal Affairs and centres and ordered them to inform the staff and not anybody in the Ministry of the Interior or the analysis department. Here we have a dispatch about SUP mentioned in Kosovska Mitrovica, and then an act, a document of the staff dating back to 1998, the 21st of October, section B, the dispatch on Kosovska Mitrovica. If you turn to the previous page, you will see the sources and basis for that assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which document --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are to be found set out there --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic -- listen to my question.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document number 12, staff document number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are saying that this document stated that the Ministry of the Interior --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a document issued by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question is, which document states that the Ministry of Interior headquarters was not to be informed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision establishing the staff sets out only the reporting between the staff and the minister himself. He set it out this way because he drafted the document. Now, in a separate document of the staff issued to -- it is a ministry decision establishing the staff which sets out that the staff is directly responsible to the minister and that it should report directly to him outside of the regular reporting system save for the routine matters. Everything that had to do with anti-terrorist documents -- anti-terrorist activities with plans for anti-terrorist activities, none of these were sent elsewhere unless they also had items referring to routine events outside of the scope of work of the MUP staff. These were reports sent up the hierarchy of the ministry, but this sort of reports were kept by the staff. I'm telling you matters that I drew upon in these various documents and on the basis of which I made these inferences. If you look at these documents, you will see that the reporting on the planned anti-terrorist activities does not include as the receiver anyone other than the minister himself. No one else in the ministry including the analysis department and various other departments are included in this reporting system which would otherwise of course have been included on all the other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic, we won't have time to go through these reports that went up. But I represent to you that the reports of the MUP staff went to the minister and to the chief of the department. Are you not aware of that? Just answer, please, are you aware that there were reports that went to the minister as well as the chief of the department and these reports were from the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These reports were not sent to the chief of the department and the minister, rather, a special direct vertical reporting channel was set up. You see, the communication between the minister and the chief could also be verbal. In these documents, however, you can't see anything testifying to that. Now, how the minister would receive reports from the staff is something that should be determined by the minister himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Milasinovic --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a bilateral reporting system. I saw reports sent to the minister. In none of these reports did I observe that on these anti-terrorist or planned activities the chief of the public security department was informed to. I did not come across any such documents or any such information that would indicate that the chief of the public security department was informed of matters related to anti-terrorist planning and activities in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, look at this document in front of you again. Here we have the chief of the department and the minister, among others, setting policy, it would seem. The current situation in Kosovo was examined in the meeting in which the duties and further engagement of members of the police were defined. How could Mr. Djordjevic be involved in defining the duties of members of the police in anti-terrorist actions without being informed about the anti-terrorist actions that they were to be involved in?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Djordjevic performed the duty of the chief of the public security department. He carried out tasks that fell within that remit. The tasks of suppressing terrorism were outside of his jurisdiction. To put it simply, his role lay more in the field of logistics and logistical support. These were technical and to a certain extent material issues which had to do with the regular activities across the territory of the republic including Kosovo and Metohija save for the duties that were conferred upon the staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. This is the situation as it was de facto and de jure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, it is really for the court to determine the situation based on the evidence. You have received information from sources we can't identify. But coming back to my question.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic here is saying that Mr. Djordjevic is involved in defining the engagement of the MUP forces in anti-terrorist operations in Belgrade. Simply, how could Mr. Djordjevic be involved in defining the engagement of the MUP forces in anti-terrorist operations without receiving information about the anti-terrorist operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said this for the simple reason because none of the documents evidenced that he was informed of these activities. He could have been informed of certain situations at meetings, but his role had nothing to do with this specific chain of command which he was outside of, and that applied to the head of the state security department too. We had this direct line to the minister who defined that the dealings were to be organised in that manner. So his role was asymmetrical.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You keep repeating --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I'm defending the gentleman. I'm merely setting out assertions based on the documents and the research I conducted in this field.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You seem to refuse to answer my question. Let me ask you this then: Having seen this document --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question then if I'm -- misunderstood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I've asked it three times, we don't have time for that. I'll ask you another one. Having seen this document, if you assume that what General Lukic reported here is true, would you now agree that General Djordjevic, on the basis of this, must have been informed about the anti-terrorist operations in Kosovo if he was involved in defining the task for the engagement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't true. He could only have been involved in logistics and certainly not in a matter which was precisely defined or specifically defined in the decision on the establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is your answer, very well. Let's look at the decision on the establishment, P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you treat that document in your report at section 3.1 which begins at page 26 in the English version, but it's section 3.1.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Should be page 26 in Serbian but --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tasks of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But -- or page 27 in Serbian. It's the section that you numbered 3 .2. That's the beginning of the part where you treat on this document, where you discuss this document. You told us that you base your conclusions on what -- or may I just put this as a question. Your conclusions that anti-terrorist police activities in Kosovo was outside of the sphere of Mr. Djordjevic after this decision was made or issued, and I think you told us that you based it on this document. In the third to last paragraph of this section of your report, section that you number 3.2, the third to last paragraph, and this is on page 29 in English, the second paragraph beginning on that page. You say: "As regards the staff for prevention of terrorism and its purview, the RJP chief according to the minister's decision retained jurisdiction only in the sphere of expert and administrative logistic support to the staff and the units engaged in performance of the task."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Retained jurisdiction only in the sphere of expert support. What does expert support mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sphere of expert or professional and administrative logistic support to the staff and the units engaged --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, expert in the sense that it can, in specific situations and not based on the competences it may have in relation to the anti-terrorist staff, rather to provide opinions on specific situations and problems related to the broader security related matters across the republic. It is important for the staff to be well aware of the activities taking place across the Republic of Serbia. However, the support was largely logistic and expert in the sense if someone had to be replaced or someone had to be dispatched or someone who is sick may be replaced because these may also have been individuals who were sent there on specific assignments given by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question dealt, Mr. Milasinovic, only about what was this expert report, and I see your answer. You are saying that --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MILASINOVIC [Resumed]
